summary: Tested HeartLink realtime messaging, presence and the new /api/conversations endpoint. Backend: 13 pytest tests (auth login via email_or_phone, /api/conversations/{user_id} shape+sort+unread, POST /api/messages -> conversations reflect immediately, /api/active-users/{user_id} presence + gender preference, WS /api/ws/{user_id} connect+ping+live delivery+delivered flag) — 13/13 PASSED. Frontend E2E (mobile 390x844, real login as shivamkks112@gmail.com): Connections page loads with Matches/Messages/Active tabs; Messages tab shows correct last-message preview, 'Now' timestamp and unread badge; Active tab shows 'Active (1)' with HeartLink Reviewer marked Online (Active(0) bug fixed for the tab content); ChatPage loads via the global wsService with no duplicate WS and no compile error; incoming message posted as User B appeared in the open chat in ~1s WITHOUT reload; outbound send via UI works; Messages tab updated inline in ~1s with new preview + unread badge; WS reconnect after 6s network offline worked (message delivered ~1s after coming back online); navigation to /discover, /likes, /notifications, /profile, /matches all render. One real residual bug: the Active tab LABEL still reads 'Active (0)' until the tab is actually clicked, because activeUsers is only fetched when activeTab==='active'.

minor.issue: Unknown user_id returns 200 [] instead of 404 (no user existence check).

Still N+1 internally: 3 awaits per match (last message aggregate, unread aggregate, user lookup) in a Python for-loop. Docstring claims 'ONE query'. Fine at current scale, but should be a single $lookup/$facet pipeline or bulk-fetch users.
The $or block has a redundant clause — {is_online:true, last_active>=thr} is fully subsumed by {last_active>=thr}, so is_online is effectively ignored in filtering (works, but dead condition).
looking_for/gender values are interpolated straight into a $regex ('^{value}$') without re.escape — a stored profile value containing regex metachars would corrupt/broaden the query.
No auth: sender_id is taken from the request body, so any caller can post messages as any user (used deliberately for this test, but it is an impersonation hole).

ui_bugs.issue: Active tab count is wrong until the tab is opened: the useEffect only calls fetchActiveUsers() when activeTab==='active', so the label renders 'Active (0)' while on Matches/Messages — this is the exact user-reported 'Active (0)' symptom. Fix: fetch active users on mount (and on the 30s interval) regardless of the selected tab.
Individual message bubbles have no data-testid (only [data-testid="messages-container"]), so message-level assertions/read receipts cannot be targeted reliably.

ui_bugs.component: Chat safety disclaimer modal ('Safety First!' / 'I Understand, Continue')
ui_bugs.issue: Modal blocking first chat entry has no data-testid on the container or the confirm button; automated flows must fall back to text matching.

eslint at line 189 previously failed compilation with "Definition for rule 'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps' was not found" (webpack compiled with 1 error). It now compiles (comment changed to // eslint-disable-line), but any re-introduction of a rule-specific disable comment will break the dev build since the react-hooks plugin is not configured.

issues: The three tabs overflow horizontally — 'Active (n)' is clipped at the right edge ('Activ...') on a 390px viewport; needs shrink/scroll-snap or shorter labels.

action_items: MatchesPage.jsx: call fetchActiveUsers() on mount (not only when the active tab is selected) so the 'Active (n)' tab label is correct — this is the remaining part of the reported Active(0) bug.
Add data-testid to chat message bubbles and to the chat safety modal + its confirm button.
Optional hardening: re.escape() the gender/looking_for regex values and remove the redundant is_online $or clause in /api/active-users.
Optional: return 404 for unknown user_id in /api/conversations/{user_id}; consider aggregating conversations in a single pipeline.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~8.3k lines; the messaging/presence/WebSocket layer (ConnectionManager, /messages, /conversations, /active-users, /ws) should be split into its own router module.
POST /api/messages trusts sender_id from the body — no JWT/session verification; same for the WebSocket path /api/ws/{user_id} which accepts any user_id and immediately marks that user online.

MatchesPage.jsx (876 lines) mixes three tab data-flows plus WS listeners in one component; the inline new_message reducer calls fetchConversations() from inside a setConversations updater (side effect inside a state updater — will double-fire under React StrictMode/concurrent rendering). A PAGEERROR 'error during concurrent rendering but React recovered' was observed on /discover.
wsService.handleMessage increments badgeCounts.unread_messages for every 'message' event including the sender's own echo, so the sender's unread badge is inflated until the next server badge_update.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (all realtime/presence/chat flows pass; Active tab label count still stale)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_realtime_iter33.py (needs websockets pkg, already installed). IMPORTANT: the backend WS event type for a new chat message is 'message' with payload {type:'message', message:{...}} — wsService re-emits it as 'new_message' to components; do not assert type=='new_message' on the socket. Profile endpoint is /api/profile/{user_id} (there is no /api/users/{id}). Chat entry shows a 'Safety First!' modal (click text 'I Understand, Continue') before [data-testid="messages-container"] is usable. Realtime verification trick: from the logged-in page, fetch()-POST /api/messages as the other user and assert the DOM updates without reload.
rca_of_the_issue: Active(0) residual: MatchesPage useEffect([activeTab]) only calls fetchActiveUsers() in the else-branch (activeTab==='active'), so activeUsers stays [] and the tab label reads 'Active (0)' while the user is on Matches/Messages; opening the tab fetches and correctly shows 'Active (1)'. Realtime messaging itself is verified working: POST /api/messages -> manager.send_message to both users with {type:'message'} -> wsService maps to 'new_message' -> ChatPage/MatchesPage inline update (~1s). Keeping ChatPage on the shared global socket fixed the previous connection-replacement problem: after navigating chat -> matches -> chat the socket stayed alive and messages continued to arrive, and the service reconnected automatically after a simulated network outage.
